decision_reason: NASA Langley releases the Kodiak nonlinear arithmetic library as open source and the current repository has build/test guidance and active source. Treat this as one library product; the Boolean Checker is an integrated module in the same repository, not a separate standalone product. The full library is licensed under its LAR-18517 NASA OSA 1.3 grant first observed with the 2020 license-folder update; the module has a distinct LAR-19222 NASA OSA 1.3 grant dating to 2017.

government_provenance.note: NASA TTP identifies the complete Kodiak software library, its nonlinear-real-arithmetic verification function, and links this exact repo. Separate NASA TTP LAR-19222-1 identifies the integrated Boolean Checker module within the same repo. This is Langley Kodiak, not the unrelated Goddard lidar also called Kodiak.

public_source.note: The repo contains the C++ nonlinear-real solver/library and its integrated Boolean Checker module, with build, test, and user documentation; these are one code family.

eligible_license.note: The core library grant is LICENSES/LAR-18517-Kodiak-NOSA-1.3.pdf, added in commit eb280290fb92dd135b25d24b83e0acf9189374e2 (2020-08-07); the separately docketed Boolean Checker module uses LICENSES/LAR-19222-Kodiak-NOSA-1.3.pdf, added with its functional source in commit 259233b62908e8e0e12c909a475581537d204830 (2017-11-28). Both documents identify NASA Open Source Agreement Version 1.3; third-party dependencies are separate.

primary_evidence.note: NASA TTP names the reusable Kodiak library and links the exact repo; repository build/test guidance provides practical use. The integrated Boolean Checker is included as a component and separately docketed under LAR-19222-1.

product_identity: NASA Langley Kodiak nonlinear arithmetic software library, including its integrated Boolean Checker module; the module is a component, not a separate product
geography: United States federal aerospace software verification and formal-methods research
license: NASA Open Source Agreement v1.3 for Kodiak core (LAR-18517; first verified grant-bearing repository snapshot 2020) and a separate NOSA v1.3 grant for Boolean Checker module LAR-19222 (first verified with 2017 module source); third-party dependencies excluded
status_note: Maintained: current NASA TTP LAR-18268-1 lists and links the exact library repo, and repository source changes continue through 2026-09-17. Catalogue once as the Langley Kodiak library; do not split its Boolean Checker module or conflate it with unrelated Goddard lidar.

decision_reason: NASA's official software catalog describes LAGER as a reusable multi-source logging system and its Download Now route links to the exact public repo. The repo provides a version file (1.0.0), CMake setup/build steps, and runnable producer/consumer examples. Its exact license separates NASA NOSA 1.3 project code from MIT-licensed reused files; the repo is quiet since 2019, so I classify the official release as archived rather than actively maintained.

government_provenance.note: NASA TTP identifies the exact LAGER logging system as an open-source NASA Johnson Space Center product and links this repository.

public_source.note: The public C++ repository has source, documentation/design files, build scripts, VERSION 1.0.0, and tested Linux/Windows build and run examples.

eligible_license.note: The exact LICENSE states NASA Open Source Agreement v1.3 for all project files except identified third-party components; reused intarweb-related files are separately MIT-licensed and cmake components retain their notices. NOSA v1.3 is OSI-approved (https://opensource.org/license/NASA-1.3). First visible project license commit d0ba01807e6c11b566e94ebd3dfc571dcf70f180 (2018-01-24) includes functional C++ source updates.

primary_evidence.note: NASA's current product page names LAGER's logging function and currently distributes the exact repository; README gives setup, build, and paired logging source/client example run instructions.

product_identity: LAGER (Light-weight Accumulator Gathering Efficiently in Real-time), a C++ logging system that sends records from multiple sources to multiple end users
geography: United States federal human-spaceflight software and logging infrastructure
license: NASA Open Source Agreement v1.3 for LAGER-authored files; explicitly identified reused intarweb code is MIT and other vendored/build files keep their separate terms
status_note: Maintained as an exact NASA TTP distribution, not active code development: the current NASA TTP record links this repository directly, while the last repository code commit is 2019-02. Do not infer ongoing code work from continued distribution.

decision_reason: The Limit Checker is a versioned, reusable NASA cFS application with official NASA catalog and Goddard cFS catalog records, a current Apache-2.0 grant, and a mission-oriented application user's guide. The repo is actively updated, with a 2026-09 source commit. The claim is scoped to LC; cFS framework dependencies are separate products/licenses.

government_provenance.note: NASA TTP identifies the exact cFS Limit Checker 2.2.0 as a NASA Goddard open-source application; NASA GSFC's cFS catalog separately describes LC's telemetry-monitoring role.

public_source.note: Public C source includes the Limit Checker application, tests, configuration, and app-specific user-guide source; GitHub shows updates through 2026-09-24.

eligible_license.note: The current repository LICENSE is Apache-2.0 for LC source; the cFE, OSAL, PSP, and other cFS framework components are required dependencies with separate source/license boundaries. The first public source plus Core Flight System NOSA document appears in commit 301b436c7cd219eae8be4cac1e3c3359e7c13096 (2017-07-01); the current Apache grant is in place by commit f320744bfa80eb1064f5bd4a3637e45c0560039f (2022-05-09).

primary_evidence.note: The NASA Goddard cFS catalog names the exact Limit Checker app and its telemetry-limit behavior; NASA's app README and generated user's guide explain configuration/operation. NASA TTP separately lists LC version 2.2.0 as a released open-source product.

product_identity: Core Flight System Limit Checker (LC) Application, a cFS plug-in that checks telemetry values against threshold/watchpoint rules and can emit events or trigger command sequences
geography: United States federal spacecraft flight-software systems
license: Current Apache-2.0 grant covers LC repository code; an earlier CFS NOSA release document and functional application source appear together in the 2017 public-release commit. cFE/OSAL/PSP and mission-specific software are separate components.
status_note: Maintained: active source activity through September 2026; NASA GSFC identifies LC among reusable cFS apps, and NASA TTP catalogs version 2.2.0. This row is the LC app, not the entire cFS bundle.

The repo contains the complete Fortran model plus its project NASA Open Source Agreement. It is explicitly end-of-life, so classify it as archived rather than active.

government_provenance.note: NASA's catalog identifies the NASA Ames Legacy Mars Global Climate Model and marks it Open Source; NASA Ames MCMC's current model-code page links the legacy source and identifies its group as the model developer.

public_source.note: The public repository has the Fortran model code, run data, tutorials, analysis/validation outputs, and detailed install, compile, run, and result-check instructions.

primary_evidence.note: The NASA Ames MCMC page, updated 2026-08-05, links users to both the Legacy GCM source and current model outputs; it also cites exact Legacy GCM research. NASA's README labels the repo an official public release.
